prsMergedThisMission.title: fix(P-177): hold Hays back from the six PARCEL-B-SLATE2 record-overlay rails
prsMergedThisMission.content: A second mid-mission finding: after both republishes, the tier1 bake was verifiably correct, but get_smart_site still served the old Mesa-Verde-collision values. Root cause: cadRollServeCutover.ts / parcelRecordAllowlist.ts overlays marketValue/assessedValue/landValue/improvementValue/livingAreaSqft/yearBuilt from hauska-engine's parcel_record_cell ledger whenever the allowlist resolves 'record' -- a gate that checks only cell coverage, never correctness. Hays' record-sourced cells for these six rails predate the crosswalk protection and reproduce the identical collision independently. Held Hays back from PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE for exactly these six rails (122 -> 116 entries), falling back to the now-correct legacy/bake value. Williamson untouched -- lexically disjoint key spaces, live-spot-verified clean. Operator-approved scope (AskUserQuestion: 'investigate and fix now').

contradictionInstrument.status: The original CTX-HAYS-KEY instrument was scratch/ephemeral (per its own close, no script was preserved in the repo) -- reconstructed here from its close file's own stated definition (served baseFacts.situsAddress vs the declared-vintage cad_property row for the SAME account, string-normalised).
contradictionInstrument.naiveBareComparison: 77,388 contradictions -- WORSE than baseline, because it compares the (correctly) crosswalk-sourced served address against the WRONG bare-prop_id account P-177 deliberately stopped using. Not a real regression; a wrong instrument.
contradictionInstrument.crosswalkCorrectComparison: 623 contradictions out of 114,121 distinct comparable nodes (128,513 raw rows, 14,392 duplicate crosswalk joins collapsed, 418 excluded for a null declared address on the correctly-matched account), joining the SAME way the bake's crosswalk does (cad_property.property_number = txgio_parcel.geo_id, ambiguity-refused). Down 98.3% from the 37,479 baseline.
contradictionInstrument.residualCharacter: Examples are city-name/road-abbreviation formatting differences on the SAME real address (e.g. served 'KYLE, TX 78640' vs declared 'BUDA, TX 78610' for the identical street number and name; 'FM 150' vs 'RR 150'), not the original class (an entirely different physical parcel's account). A stricter string-normaliser (city/road-abbreviation aware) would likely close most of this residual; not attempted here.
contradictionInstrument.honestCaveat: This is a reconstructed instrument, not the original. 623 is not independently cross-checked against a second implementation the way the original close's own scanH was. Report this number as informative, not as re-certifying the original instrument's own precision.

missionPremise: The overseer review (2026-09-13, _inbox/2026-09-13_p175_overseer_review.md) found P-175's own crosswalk fix never reached the served polygon: node 48209:97658 after P-175's publish still carried Mesa Verde's label/dollars, because P-175's fix only affected the resolver's SEARCH-time routing, never the tier1 BAKE's own account-attribute lookup (which stayed keyed by the node's bare TxGIO prop_id -- coincidentally a real, different CAD account for gate-blocked Hays). The overseer's Option A ruling: the TxGIO-keyed node IS the canonical Hays node (it has the geometry and cells); only its account-derived attributes need crosswalk correction, in the bake, not a new identity scheme.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this close by: (1) reading the four merged PRs' diffs directly; (2) running node --test test/publish.test.mjs in hauska-factory and confirming the 4 new cadroll-gate tests pass; (3) running npx vitest run src/lib/parcelRecordAllowlist.test.ts in legacy-design-tools and confirming the 48/48 including the new Hays-holdback falsifier; (4) live-reading 48209:97658/97651/97652/97653/97657 via get_smart_site and confirming market values in the 50,130-50,390 band with no Mesa Verde attributes; (5) running node scripts/surface-probe.mjs --rows P-175 from this doc_repo worktree and confirming it still reads FAIL 5 for the reason named in realSurfaceProbeFinding, not a different reason. If any of those disagrees with what is written here, this close is wrong.
scopeBasis: The dispatch named exactly one fix location (nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts) and one explicit out-of-scope boundary (Option B, minting new CAD-PropertyID-keyed nodes, stays with P-124/OPS-21). Two further defect-mechanism discoveries were made live-verifying the dispatch's OWN falsifiers, and fixed only with explicit operator approval at each step (the cadroll-gate fix, and the parcel-record-slate holdback) -- both scoped as narrowly as the original fix (gate-blocked counties only, Williamson excluded from the second fix on positive evidence it doesn't share the defect). A THIRD and FOURTH mechanism (Property Explorer's ledger reader, and structuralFactRead.ts) were found and diagnosed but deliberately NOT fixed, per explicit operator decision, because fixing the dominant one (the ledger reader) requires writing into a live, separately-governed store in a third repo whose current, sanctioned writer pipeline was not located, and whose obvious script is explicitly frozen by a standing 2026-08-26 ruling this lane has no authority to override. Retirement of the 5 named hollow account-keyed snapshots was completed as instructed, with its non-durability and the absence of any serve-time decline mechanism reported honestly rather than assumed.
